summary.headline: Aptus Pharma H1 FY27 revenue rose to Rs 48.90 crore from Rs 14.38 crore, with PAT of about Rs 5.08 crore; no forward guidance given.
summary.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 (half-year ended 30 September 2026) revenue from operations of about Rs 48.90 crore versus Rs 14.38 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of about Rs 7.68 crore, PBT of about Rs 6.83 crore and PAT of about Rs 5.08 crore. Management stressed working capital discipline, with inventory of about Rs 16.25 crore and trade receivables of about Rs 28.64 crore against total assets of about Rs 54.55 crore. The strategy was reiterated as three pillars: manufacturing (about 20% of portfolio self-made by March 2028), pan-India expansion (46% geographic coverage by March 2027, pan-India by 2029) and international expansion. Management declined to give any quantitative guidance on revenue, EBITDA, PAT or capex returns during the Q&A.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 14.38 crore in H1 FY26

segments.name: Acute therapy
segments.commentary: Largest revenue contributor at about 44% of sales.

segments.name: Chronic and semi-chronic therapy
segments.commentary: About 20% of sales; management said the chronic division was introduced last year and will be strengthened (cardio, diabetes cited).

segments.name: Wellness and OTC
segments.commentary: About 20% of sales; management called it doing extremely well and a focus area.

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: About 16% of revenue; the vertical is meant to build international opportunities.

guidance_outlook: No forward guidance on topline, EBITDA or PAT margins for the next one to three years; management said it will disclose guidance after compliance review.
Target of 46% geographic coverage across India by March 2027.
Manufacturing expansion targeted by March 2028, with about 20% of the product portfolio made in-house, mainly for self-consumption with the rest for rest-of-world export.
Long-term objective of a pan-India footprint by 2029, with every medical store (cited as over 8.5 lakh) to carry Aptus products.
International expansion to be gradual and opportunity-led in selected markets across Asia, Africa and Latin America.
capex_capacity: Initial manufacturing capex planned at about Rs 35 crore; management said Rs 25 crore will be funded from the ongoing preferential issue, with the rest arranged as needed.
Capex to start only after the exchange grants necessary approval for the preferential issue; a detailed project report has been submitted to authorities.
No commissioning timeline or peak revenue potential from the capex was disclosed.
Company says it will not pursue CDMO; plant is intended for self-consumption and rest-of-world export.
demand_pricing: Portfolio of more than 300 formulations across acute, chronic, wellness and OTC; more than 250 distributors and sub-distributors; retail availability exceeding 45k outlets; more than 10,000 doctors cited as users.
Prescription-led model; management said it is not dependent on a single product and cited diversified portfolio as the key USP.
Field force of 142 on-roll medical representatives, with more than 150 on-roll and off-roll professionals and 200-plus distribution sales representatives; attrition stated below 5-6%.
Gross margins described as good in the pharma industry; no product-level pricing or realisation data given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the guidelines for topline, EBITDA and PAT margin over the next two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not giving any forward figures or guidance on EBITDA, topline or bottom line at present.

qa_highlights.question: What is the company's USP versus competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a diversified portfolio across acute, chronic, OTC and wellness, an experienced promoter team, and strong marketing and distribution networks.

qa_highlights.question: Will manufacturing be CDMO or own formulations, and how is the Rs 35 crore capex funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not do CDMO; the plant is for self-consumption (about 20% of products) with the rest for rest-of-world export. Rs 25 crore will come from the preferential issue, with the balance arranged as needed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue potential and completion timeline of the Rs 35 crore capex, and will margins be higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify revenue potential or completion timing, saying it would not give figures now; it said gross margins in pharma are good.

qa_highlights.question: How many marketing employees does the company have and what is attrition?
qa_highlights.answer: 142 on-roll medical representatives, 150-plus on-roll and off-roll professionals and 200-plus distribution sales representatives; attrition below 5-6%.

risks_watch: Working capital intensity: receivables of about Rs 28.64 crore are larger than inventory-plus-cash-type buffers suggest against total assets of about Rs 54.55 crore; collection efficiency to be tracked.
Execution risk on manufacturing capex (about Rs 35 crore, Rs 25 crore via preferential issue) with no commissioning timeline or return figures disclosed.
No quantitative guidance, limiting ability to assess sustainability of H1 growth against a low prior-year base of Rs 14.38 crore.
Reliance on third-party WHO-GMP manufacturers for current product supply.
Geographic expansion (46% coverage by March 2027) and international plans lack detail on infrastructure and funding.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and vision but cautious and evasive on numbers: management repeatedly declined to give guidance or capex returns, deferring figures until compliance clearance. Tone emphasises phased, disciplined execution and working capital management.
key_quotes: As management, we do not view the performance only through the lens of revenue growth.
We believe that sustainable value creation comes from building a strong business step-by-step rather than pursuing expansion without considering the financial and operational implications.
We will therefore follow a gradual and opportunity lead approach rather than pursuing expansion simply to increase the number of the countries in which we operate.

adds.what: Initial manufacturing plant (about 20% of portfolio self-made by March 2028), capex about Rs 35 crore

growth.why: No numeric revenue, EBITDA or PAT guidance was given; management declined forward figures, citing compliance review. Only a 46% India coverage target by March 2027 and a Rs 35 crore manufacturing capex (Rs 25 crore via preferential issue, start pending exchange approval, no commissioning timeline) were stated, so backing is vague.
